policy: Exact component literature adoptions after legacy reviewed supplements. Preserve replaced values and complete previous evidence. Shared model ages and adopted temperatures are explicitly scoped; never copy unresolved spectra or total masses into individual measurements.

bright-spica.note: Resolved Spica primary/secondary solution from Table 7. Spectroscopic temperatures and binary-model radii/luminosities retain formal errors and model assumptions. The shared 12.5 +/- 1 Myr evolutionary age is not an independent component age; no Ac properties are inferred.

age_gyr.scope: Shared coeval close-binary model age; not an independent age measurement for each star.

spectral_type.scope: Component classification from the confirmed inner binary branch, explicitly normalized to literature Aa/Ab; not the uncertain intermediate occultation branch.

msc-07346+3153-c.note: YY Gem A/B follow the publication phase-zero primary convention, mapped to MSC Ca/Cb. New dynamical masses use the adopted eclipsing inclination; radii are volume-equivalent tomographic model results. The 3800 K value is the explicitly adopted common atmosphere parameter, not two independent measured temperatures. Luminosity is Stefan-Boltzmann scaling using those adopted model inputs; unresolved C flux and Gaia single-source radius/luminosity remain separate source observations.

age_gyr.scope: Castor coeval-system age inferred from Aa, shared with the physically associated YY Gem pair; not a separate YY Gem age measurement.

bright-nunki.note: Approximate individual isochrone mass and radius from Waisberg et al. 2025, explicitly retained by Waisberg & Katz 2026 sections 3.1 and 4.1. No formal individual errors supplied. The 14.6 +/- 1.8 solar-mass dynamical result is the total binary mass with two-sigma bounds; it is not assigned to either star. The approximately 18500 K line-ratio result is combined-spectrum evidence, not an independent component temperature. Withheld individual fields: luminosity_solar.

bright-menkalinan.note: Updated beta Aur primary/secondary solution from Jonak et al. 2026. Adopt rounded Table 8 values and profile-likelihood errors, rather than the smaller formal MCMC errors in Table 6. Primary temperature is fixed to the earlier 9350 K calibration; secondary temperature follows the new fitted ratio and retains that calibration uncertainty. Original Southworth 2007 measurements and provenance are retained. Catalog astrometric distance remains unchanged pending a separate motion/distance review.

luminosity_solar.section: Stefan-Boltzmann scaling from updated radius and adopted temperature
luminosity_solar.scope: Derived equivalent bolometric luminosity; no new direct flux measurement. Temperature calibration dominates the error.
